title: Find the Maximum Number of Fruits Collected
summary: A game dungeon is composed of n x n rooms, where each room (i, j) contains a certain number of fruits represented by fruits[i][j].
statement: A game dungeon is composed of n x n rooms, where each room (i, j) contains a certain number of fruits represented by fruits[i][j]. Three children start their journey from the corner rooms (0, 0), (0, n - 1), and (n - 1, 0) and each must make exactly n - 1 moves to reach the room (n - 1, n - 1). The movement rules for each child are as follows: - The child starting at (0, 0) can move to (i + 1, j + 1), (i + 1, j), or (i, j + 1) if the target room exists. - The child starting at (0, n - 1) can move to (i + 1, j - 1), (i + 1, j), or (i + 1, j + 1) if the target room exists. - The child starting at (n - 1, 0) can move to (i - 1, j + 1), (i, j + 1), or (i + 1, j + 1) if the target room exists. Each time a child enters a room, they collect all the fruits in that room, and the room is emptied if another child enters. The goal is to determine the maximum number of fruits the children can collect from the dungeon.
constraints: fruits is an n by n nonnegative matrix with 2 <= n <= 1,000.
Three children start at the top-left, top-right, and bottom-left and make exactly n-1 allowed moves to bottom-right.
A room’s fruit counts once even if several children visit it; maximize the collected total.
hints: Exactly n-1 moves force the top-left child to follow the main diagonal.
The other children remain in disjoint triangles until the shared destination, so optimize their paths independently.
Run row-wise DP above the diagonal and column-wise DP below it; add both pre-destination scores to the diagonal sum.
Triangle separation prevents double counting, and each DP transition enumerates the three legal predecessor positions.
editorial: Triangle separation prevents double counting, and each DP transition enumerates the three legal predecessor positions.

tests.explanation: The diagonal child and optimal upper-right and lower-left paths collect ten distinct rooms totaling 100.
The starts and shared destination cover all four rooms exactly once.
